title: Interference: whose fix is it?
idea: First make sure your own station is clean. When a neighbor's radio or TV picks you up, the fix usually goes at their receiver: a filter at its antenna input, or properly installed connectors.

rows: Your signal gets into a neighbor's radio or TV
Their receiver: a filter at its antenna input
Their TV: first check the feed line connectors are installed properly
Your station: check it works properly and doesn't bother your own TV on the same channel
A nearby FM broadcast station gets into your 2 m radio
A device in a neighbor's home interferes with you
Together: find the device, mention the FCC rules politely, and check your own station

cards.t: A filter at the antenna input of the neighbor's radio, to block your signal
cards.why: Blocking the amateur signal at the affected receiver's antenna input can reduce the interference.

cards.t: Check the TV feed line connectors are installed properly
cards.why: That's the first step for cable TV interference that isn't fiber optic.

cards.t: Make sure your station works properly and doesn't interfere with your own TV on the same channel
cards.why: That's the first thing to do when a neighbor reports interference.

cards.t: A band-reject filter on your 2 m radio, against a nearby commercial FM station
cards.why: Here your radio is the one being interfered with, so the filter goes on it.

cards.t: Make sure your station meets the standards of good amateur practice
cards.why: Do this when a neighbor's device is interfering with you, too.

cards.t: Work with your neighbor to find the device causing interference to you
cards.why: When something in their home interferes with you, start by finding it together.

cards.t: Politely tell your neighbor that FCC rules prohibit devices that cause interference
cards.why: That's part of the right approach, along with finding the device and checking your own station.

traps.wrong: The microphone gain of the transmitter is turned up too high
traps.why: Mic gain affects your own audio. A broadcast radio picks you up because it can't reject strong signals outside its band.
Harmonics are one cause, but so are fundamental overload and spurious emissions. It's all of them.

traps.wrong: Block the interfering signal with a filter on the amateur transmitter
traps.why: The fix the pool wants is at the affected receiver: block the amateur signal at its antenna input.

traps.wrong: Immediately turn off your transmitter and contact the nearest FCC office for assistance
traps.why: Don't shut down and call the FCC. First check your station works properly and doesn't interfere with your own TV.
A preamplifier makes overload worse. A band-reject filter blocks the FM station.

traps.wrong: Work with your neighbor to identify the offending device
traps.why: Working with your neighbor is one part. Telling them the rules politely and checking your own station are too.

traps.wrong: Add a preamplifier to the TV antenna input
traps.why: A preamplifier doesn't fix interference. First check the TV feed line connectors are installed properly.
